key_physical_insights.torque_vs_rotational_speed: Hyperbolic relationship governed by power (P = tau * omega). Failures cluster at the physical extremes: high torque with low speed (stalling/overstrain) or low torque with extreme speed (overpower/runaway).
key_physical_insights.thermal_dissipation: Heat dissipation failures occur when ambient air temperature is high and the process-to-air temperature gradient is suppressed (< 8.9 K), preventing adequate motor cooling.
key_physical_insights.tool_wear_fatigue: Tool wear exhibits progressive degradation. Machine failures heavily skew toward higher wear durations (failure median 180.5 min vs normal median 107.0 min), particularly when coupled with elevated torque loads.
key_physical_insights.correlation_vs_causation_caveat: Torque (r = +0.19) and Tool Wear (r = +0.11) show positive linear correlation with failure, while Rotational Speed (r = -0.04) shows mild negative correlation. However, linear correlation understates these relationships because failure boundaries are non-linear (e.g. power limits and thermal dissipation limits).
